key_forensic_finding: The OPEN worlds enter a high-churn, low-syntactic-reuse regime at only 35.8%-42.2% of the elimination sequence while 44-55 support variables remain. Their worst completed Shannon step creates 151,529-513,989 nodes, versus 27,047-56,777 in the four PASS worlds. Hash-cons hits per created node fall from 1.40%-6.16% on PASS worlds to 0.031%-0.068% on OPEN worlds.
scientific_interpretation: R19's frontier is an intermediate representation-growth wall. Three of four OPEN worlds meet the preregistered temporary-churn rule; W06 additionally exhibits retained-node growth to 929,392 live nodes. The common signature is low reuse of syntactically canonical AND/OR subgraphs. This motivates testing stronger function-level canonicalization, not increasing R19 limits or retuning its logic.
claim_ceiling: No asymptotic complexity law, arbitrary-CNF totality, SAT-in-P, P=NP, or P!=NP conclusion.
